title: Dispatch OGF 1: Glass Fruit Draws Crowds to Alderwick Market
summary: Scenes visible inside the new harvest appear to show moments no stranger could know.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The first glass pears from Rill Orchard reached the market yesterday. They have the weight and scent of ordinary fruit, but their skins are nearly transparent. Held to a lamp, each contains a small scene with figures, buildings, and a distinct horizon. The scenes move only when the fruit is turned.

Mrs. Elspeth Rill, who has tended the northern orchard for thirty years, says the crop began on three trees after a late frost. She offered six pears for sale before buyers began calling her back to the stall. One woman found a scene of her brother repairing a blue toy boat in their childhood kitchen. The brother died last winter. Neither Mrs. Rill nor her workers had met him.

A purchaser who asked not to be named saw herself burning a letter behind a locked bedroom door. She bought the pear and asked the market inspector to remove the remaining fruit from public display. Mr. Joseph Fenner, whose stall faces Mrs. Rill’s, says the request drew more spectators than the fruit itself.

Dr. Lenora Saye of the Eidetical Institute examined one pear without cutting it. The image could not be projected onto paper. Through a comparison lens, however, the tiny room inside the fruit extended farther than its skin. Dr. Saye called it “an observed place folded into a thing small enough to carry.”

Mrs. Rill has suspended sales. She says her trees have produced no fruit like this before and will not invite strangers to inspect the orchard until she knows whether the scenes belong to the people who see them.
